lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: washer and dryer safety

objective: With an adult, learners practice three specific washer/dryer safety behaviors (checking pockets before loading, not overloading the machine, and never reaching into a running machine) across two supported rounds, then explain why each behavior matters.
scenario: With a trusted adult present at the washer and dryer, the learner practices loading a wash following three safety behaviors, first with the adult narrating each check, then a second time with the learner leading and the adult confirming.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult must be present for the entire loading and starting process.
Hands stay clear of the drum at all times while the machine is running.
Stop and ask the adult for help if the machine makes an unfamiliar noise or shows an error.

simulationAlternative.description: If no washer or dryer is available in the home, the learner instead reviews a labeled diagram or short adult-led walkthrough of a washer and dryer (at a laundromat, a relative's home, or a printed diagram) and, with the adult, verbally walks through where and how each of the three checks would happen, then explains each check's purpose the same way as the real-machine reflection.

tasks.directions: Before practicing, name one thing you think could go wrong if someone loaded a washer or dryer without checking it first.
With your adult, load one wash following three checks: pockets checked and emptied, load size checked against the machine's fill line, and hands kept clear of the drum while it's running.

prompts.text: I checked every pocket on every item before loading.
I checked the load against the fill line rather than guessing.
I did not reach into the machine at any point while it was running.
My adult was present for the entire loading and starting process.

tasks.directions: Lead a second wash load yourself, with your adult present to confirm, running through the same three checks without being told each one.

prompts.text: Which of the three checks did you remember on your own without a reminder, and which one did your adult have to prompt you on?
Pick one of the three safety behaviors and explain, in your own words, exactly what could go wrong if that specific check were skipped — not just 'it's dangerous,' but what would actually happen.

remediation: If the learner skips the pocket check specifically, reteach with a five-item practice pile where at least two items have something small hidden in a pocket, and have the learner find both before moving to a real load.
extension: Have the learner teach the three safety behaviors to a younger sibling or family member, with the adult present to confirm the teaching is accurate.
